Faia's Notes & Chords Explorer

Meet the creator

Hi, I’m Faia.

I retired from the U.S. Navy, and now I’m a music producer, composer, and student in Full Sail University’s Music Production bachelor’s program. After completing my Audio Production associate degree, I continued my education to deepen my skills in songwriting, production, arranging, mixing, and music for visual media.

I created Faia’s Notes & Chords Explorer to make music theory more approachable, visual, and interactive. The app helps learners identify notes and chord tones, understand chord quality and Roman-numeral function, practice recommended keyboard fingering, and measure progress through structured tests. No personal information is stored or collected, and the app is completely free to use. Please support my work by following my YouTube channel and checking out my music on YouTube Music.

Faia's Notes & Chords Explorer

Explore notes, chords, and scales: choose a chord, analyze its Roman-numeral function in any major or minor key, explore related chords on the circle of fifths, play it through the built-in synth or an external VST/AU host, and see recommended piano finger numbers, learn and practice essential scales with fingering guidance, and measure your progress with Beginner, Moderate, and Expert automatically scored test levels.

A browser cannot load AU or VST plug-ins directly. External mode sends MIDI to a DAW or plug-in host, where you select the AU/VST instrument.

How to use
  1. Enter your name on the welcome screen. It will identify your test sessions and reports.
  2. Select the chord and the key in which you want to analyze it, or open the Scales Lab to study and practice scales.
  3. Review the Roman numeral, relative pair, diatonic chords, circle-of-fifths position, and recommended fingering. Choose right hand, left hand, both hand options, or automatic fingering.
  4. Use Built-in browser instrument for immediate sound.
  5. For an AU/VST, select External MIDI, choose a virtual MIDI bus, then load the instrument in your DAW or plug-in host.
  6. For a scored session, select Beginner, Moderate, or Expert, choose 10, 20, or 30 questions, then select the question content.
  7. Beginner emphasizes natural notes and foundational chords; Moderate adds accidentals, chord symbols, and seventh chords; Expert adds exact-octave notes, the full chord library, and Roman-numeral function questions.
  8. The app scores a complete answer automatically. An incorrect or incomplete answer reveals the correct keys and finger numbers, then advances after seven seconds.
  9. The seven-second answer-review period is excluded from active answer time, average response time, and pace calculations.
  10. When finished, export a print-friendly HTML report or use Print / Save PDF.
